items.text: Final results of the [[e:2026 Israeli legislative election]] give [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]]'s bloc 53 seats, [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s bloc 48 and Arab-led parties a record 19. President [[p:Isaac Herzog]] accepted the certified results on 4 Nov and opened consultations; Ra'am says it will recommend Eisenkot.

Tehran says its seven-step plan to reopen the the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks could now be done in two days rather than a week, after Supreme Leader [[p:Mojtaba Khamenei]] gave the government more power to negotiate (IRNA). Iran still demands an end to the US naval blockade and sanctions; Qatar and Pakistan mediate.
items.notes: Iranian officials' claims; no confirmed change in demands.

items.text: US envoy [[p:Steve Witkoff]] announced US-mediated working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, covering post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian steps. US officials will first meet French, German, British, EU and NATO representatives in Brussels.

Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese diplomats and closed Sudan's consulate in Asosa, two days after Khartoum complained to the UN Security Council and the African Union that Ethiopia lets the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]] launch drones from its soil. Ethiopia denies this and accuses Sudan's army of backing [[p:Tigray People's Liberation Front|TPLF]]-linked rebels.

Democrats swept the [[e:2026 United States elections|midterm elections]]: CBS projects they won the House and at least 54 Senate seats, flipping Texas, South Carolina, Kansas, Maine, Iowa, Ohio and North Carolina. Alaska and Mississippi were still uncalled on 4 Nov, and [[p:Hakeem Jeffries]] expects at least 255 House seats.

Republican fallout: Speaker [[p:Mike Johnson]] won't run to lead House Republicans next term, and [[p:Steve Scalise]] is running for minority leader. Vice President [[p:JD Vance]] wrote that the war with Iran lost the election, while [[p:Donald Trump]] blamed the candidates and said he accepts the results. Exit polls put Trump's approval at 38%.

After the midterm losses, Trump told the Financial Times he has no immediate plans to strike Iran but is "ready" to escalate. Bloomberg says the weeks before the new Congress sits in January carry a high risk of escalation. Brent fell almost 2% to about $101.70, and House Democrats say they will try to end the war and the tariffs.
items.reporter: Omar Tamo, Eltaf Najafizada, Fiona MacDonald

items.text: Democrats won governorships in Texas (Gina Hinojosa beat [[p:Greg Abbott]]), Ohio (Amy Acton beat [[p:Vivek Ramaswamy]]), Georgia and Iowa. Republican [[p:Byron Donalds]] won Florida.

[[p:Mark Carney]] says "more intense" trade talks with Washington have begun, with the US asking less and offering more, after a call with Trump on 1 Nov. Talks broke down in August, after which the US put a 50% tariff on $20bn of Canadian goods.

Mexico's push for a bilateral trade deal before the midterms ended without an announcement. [[p:Claudia Sheinbaum]] reports progress on non-tariff barriers, but there is no relief from US Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium and cars. Latin Times says Mexico is now reshaping its strategy for a Democratic Congress.

[[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]] left Brazil: Argentine migration records show him crossing into Puerto Iguazú with his family late on 27 Oct, then boarding a private jet that filed for Guayaquil but landed in Miami. Brazil's foreign ministry summoned Argentina's chargé d'affaires on 29 Oct. Buenos Aires now says the matter is closed.
items.notes: Brazil suspects Argentine officials helped; no official confirmation (Times Brasil).

items.text: At least 22 electoral abuse cases ([[e:2026 Brazilian general election|2026 election]]) remain open at the [[p:Superior Electoral Court]]: 15 cite Lula and 7 cite Flávio Bolsonaro. No ruling date is set, and a lawyer says they could run past the inauguration.
items.notes: Outlets differ on the count (18, 20 or 22).

items.text: Brazil's central bank paused its rate cuts, holding the Selic at 13.75%.

Acting president [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]] again promised elections under a renewed electoral authority with international observers, but gave no date and tied them to legal and judicial reforms. [[p:María Corina Machado]], back from exile since 25 Oct, demands an electoral calendar.

[[p:Marco Rubio]] met Venezuela's new foreign minister, Oliver Blanco, in Washington, urged more releases of political prisoners and restated Trump's three-phase plan for the country. Blanco then met [[p:Scott Bessent]] about rejoining the international financial system. Primicias reports Washington last week backed a roadmap letting Rodríguez declare the presidency vacant in 2027, opening a six-month window to call elections.
items.notes: Meeting confirmed by State Dept and Treasury readouts; the 2027 roadmap detail is reported, not independently checked.

items.text: The Turkish floating power plant Erol Bey (63 MW) left Havana, EFE reports, leaving one [[p:Karpowership]] unit in Cuba. Blackouts exceed 20 hours a day in Havana and can last three days in the provinces. Havana partly blames US limits on oil supplies.

El Salvador has sent more than 2,000 troops to Haiti to find four Salvadoran technicians missing since a gang attack on 18 Oct; the UN says only about 200 serve under the [[p:Gang Suppression Force]]. [[p:Nayib Bukele]] posted videos of helicopters firing on gangs. The leader of the [[p:400 Mawozo]] gang wrote to the UN seeking talks.
items.notes: Bukele's combat videos not independently verified.

items.text: An explosives-laden truck blew up near a police station in El Tambo, Cauca, killing one and wounding two. No group has claimed it. President [[p:Abelardo de la Espriella]] ordered security forces to find those responsible, amid a wave of drone attacks on police.
Civil society groups condemned the killing of former anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa and blamed anti-democratic groups.
items.notes: From an EFE news digest; full article not read.

items.text: Indec's living-conditions survey counts 9.7 million people in poverty out of about 30 million measured (Clarín).
The Ueno Bank scandal led the central bank chief to resign. Congress is debating faster deposit recovery, and there is a push for impeachment.
President José Antonio Kast met Pope Leo XIV, then travelled to Madrid for the Ibero-American Summit while a truckers' strike continues at home.
A judge in Manta reinstated the trial of 46 crew from two boats bombed by the US in the Pacific, who are accused of drug-trafficking links.
President Keiko Fujimori marked 100 days in office, focusing on organised crime and preparations for El Niño.
